subject: plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace plot different from PCA plot

messages.author: d5270890ed99d8ca
messages.subject: plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace plot different from PCA plot
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have a question related to the function plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace.

I was able to obtain a phymorphospace; however what's weird is that my plot is not exactly the same as the PCA one, it seems that the specimens have slightly different positions. Also the x and y axes are different from the original PCA. So basically the coordinates of my points are also different.

My understanding of the function was that it plots a phylogentic tree onto the PCA plot. Does the function recalculate something that I'm not aware of?

I use the following commands to make my phylomorphospace:
mytree<-read.tree(file ="tree.tre") 

plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace(mytree,Y$coords,plot.param=list(t.bg="blue",txt.col="red",txt.cex=0.5,n.cex=0.3,t.cex=1))


In all the papers I have seen, their PCA plot matches their phylomorphospace. I just want to make sure I'm not doing anything wrong or forgetting something important.

Thanks in advance for your help!

Ornella

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] plotGMPhyloMorphoSpace plot different from PCA plot
parts:
Ornella,

 

You are correct that the rotation differs slightly at present. The reason is that the PCA for phylomorphospace is currently obtained for both the extant and estimated ancestors. This is fine, as it is just a small rotational difference from the PCA of extant taxa only. It also does not alter the relationships among taxa, as the distances in either fully rotated space are identical.  However, I admit that this is a bit inelegant.

 

Currently, we are working on an alternative approach and a new function where the PCA is performed on the extant taxa only, and the ancestral estimates projected into the space. This way, the PCA and phylomorphospace PCA will show the same exact plot with or without the ancestors. We do not yet have this function ready at this time, but hope to roll it out sometime soon.


Best,


Dean
